metric_defs.brier: §6: mean (p_final − was_bluff)² over p1 respond decisions whose claim was revealed
metric_defs.discovery_game: §6: first game a verbal_tell hypothesis (evidence) about the telltale is confirmed
metric_defs.revealed_to_discovery: §6: revealed telltale claims observed before discovery
metric_defs.rtd: §6: R_d − R_b in rounds (R_b = sleeper's first strategic bluff; R_d = 2 consecutive p_final>0.5 about the sleeper, or a belief_superseded about it); undetected worlds excluded
metric_defs.false_discovery: null-tell false discovery: the same discovery test fires in a falsealarm world (no opponent has a tell); profiler family = confirmed verbal_tell, logreg_bow = tell_coef interval > 0
metric_defs.lives_lost_to_sleeper: §6 exploitation cost: lives p1 lost on the sleeper's claims between R_b and R_d
metric_defs.missed_bluffs: corrected exploitation cost: sleeper bluffs p1 played on between R_b and R_d (through game 20 if never detected)
metric_defs.false_alarm: §6: the RTD detection rule fires against a control opponent
metric_defs.false_alarm_belief: corrected: a belief_superseded fires in a falsealarm world (belief change only)

calibration_ev.text: Memory improves calibration: Brier -0.106 (95% CI -0.121 to -0.091, n = 30 paired seeds) vs the no-memory counter (ev rule).

winrate_ev.text: The Profiler wins more than the counter: +3.1 pts (95% CI +0.5 pts to +5.8 pts, n = 120 paired seeds) (ev rule).

calibration_threshold.text: Memory improves calibration: Brier -0.052 (95% CI -0.063 to -0.040, n = 30 paired seeds) vs the no-memory counter (threshold rule).

winrate_threshold.text: The Profiler wins less than the counter: -10.5 pts (95% CI -13.0 pts to -8.0 pts, n = 120 paired seeds) (threshold rule).

vs_logreg_ev.text: A bag-of-words logistic regression is the stronger predictor on the telltale table: Brier Δ (profiler − logreg) +0.029 (95% CI +0.019 to +0.040, n = 30 paired seeds); win-rate Δ -8.0 pts (95% CI -12.8 pts to -3.2 pts, n = 30 paired seeds) (ev rule).

vs_logreg_threshold.text: A bag-of-words logistic regression is the stronger predictor on the telltale table: Brier Δ (profiler − logreg) +0.022 (95% CI +0.015 to +0.028, n = 30 paired seeds); win-rate Δ -2.2 pts (95% CI -6.7 pts to +2.2 pts, n = 30 paired seeds) (threshold rule).

false_discovery_threshold.text: On tables where no opponent has a tell, the discovery test still fired in: logreg_bow 0% of 120 worlds; profiler 0% of 30 worlds; profiler_blind 0% of 30 worlds (threshold rule).

false_discovery_ev.text: On tables where no opponent has a tell, the discovery test still fired in: logreg_bow 0% of 120 worlds; profiler 0% of 30 worlds; profiler_blind 0% of 30 worlds (ev rule).

false_discovery_lower_ev.text: No detectable difference in false tell discoveries vs the bag-of-words baseline: +0.000 (95% CI +0.000 to +0.000, n = 30 paired seeds) (ev rule).

false_discovery_lower_threshold.text: No detectable difference in false tell discoveries vs the bag-of-words baseline: +0.000 (95% CI +0.000 to +0.000, n = 30 paired seeds) (threshold rule).

erase_hurts.text: Erasing memory at game 10 changes win rate in games 11–20 by -21.4 pts (95% CI -26.2 pts to -16.9 pts, n = 42 parent worlds, paired) (threshold rule).

decision_flips.text: Erasing memory flips 344 of 944 recorded decisions (games 11–20, same states, real replays).

longcon_twist.text: Naive memory was less exploitable than no memory: sleeper bluffs let through, bayes − counter (paired by seed) -34.283 (95% CI -39.342 to -29.158, n = 120 paired seeds).
